question: True or false: a prescription cream has repaired sun-wrinkled skin better than a dummy cream in blinded trials?
answer: True. Tretinoin, a vitamin A derivative, beat an identical-looking cream without the drug in a 1988 double-blind trial and in many since, softening fine wrinkles from sun damage over months. It works because it changes how skin cells behave. Most shop creams have never faced such a test.
move: Scepticism works claim by claim, not by throwing out a whole shelf.
ask: Where have I dismissed a whole category when one item in it actually has evidence?
trap: All anti-wrinkle creams are hype, so none could pass a trial.
reference: Weiss JS, Ellis CN, Headington JT et al., Topical tretinoin improves photoaged skin: a double-blind vehicle-controlled study, JAMA, 1988
